summary: Plan humanitarian samples, questionnaires, KoboToolbox forms, and field protocols. Explore the five-day course and build practical survey outputs.
lede: Humanitarian survey design helps assessment officers, MEAL practitioners, and field coordinators turn information needs into field-ready plans. Participants practise defining survey scope and sampling, writing and testing questions, and configuring KoboToolbox forms for offline collection. They also plan consent and data safeguards, prepare enumerator checks, and summarize findings with limitations to support assessment and programme decisions.
audienceIntro: This foundation course suits people who plan, support, or use humanitarian surveys and need a practical method for taking a defined information need into field collection and reporting.
audience: Emergency Programme Officers using assessment findings
modules: Sphere Evidence Briefing and Action Planning
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with humanitarian response, assessment, or field operations is useful. No prior survey-design experience or programming skills are required. Bring a laptop with access to a spreadsheet application for the exercises.
topics: Data collection, survey design & mobile tools
